items.headline: Mexico opens with dominant 2-0 win
items.body: Mexico defeated South Africa 2-0 in the tournament opener at Azteca Stadium. South Africa's Sphephelo Sithole received the first red card of the tournament, becoming only the fourth player sent off in a World Cup opening match. The first two group stage matches averaged 2.5 goals per match.

items.headline: 48-team format expands knockout stage
items.body: The expanded tournament features 12 groups of four teams with top two advancing, plus eight best third-place teams advancing to a new Round of 32. Group stage runs June 11-27 with all matches using dynamic pricing for tickets.

items.headline: Brazil faces attacking void without Rodrygo
items.body: Rodrygo ruled out with torn ACL and meniscus from March injury. Estêvão also unavailable with hamstring tear; Carlo Ancelotti's side missing two key attacking players. Neymar showing positive progress in calf recovery but unlikely for opener vs Morocco.

items.headline: Spain's Yamal racing against time
items.body: Lamine Yamal dealing with groin and hamstring issues, hasn't played since April 22. Coach Luis de la Fuente indicated Yamal on track for Cape Verde opener but likely minutes-restricted. Nico Williams and Victor Munoz also managing injuries.

items.headline: Argentina's Messi fit after hamstring
items.body: Lionel Messi recovered from hamstring injury, played final 20 minutes against Iceland and scored penalty. Argentina won both warm-ups with shutouts vs Honduras and Iceland. Defending champions on track for tournament.

items.headline: Canada's Davies questionable for opener
items.body: Alphonso Davies returned to full training after hamstring injury but confirmed out for Bosnia and Herzegovina match. Star left-back critical to Canada's Group B hopes. Club teammate Serge Gnabry ruled out entirely for Germany.

items.headline: England's depth tested by absences
items.body: Bukayo Saka managing Achilles issue with restricted training but expected to feature. Cole Palmer omitted due to poor form at Chelsea. Thomas Tuchel monitoring veteran stars while building around key attacking weapons.

items.headline: Netherlands loses Timber, De Ligt, Simons
items.body: Dutch defensive options severely compromised. Jurrien Timber unavailable despite recovery efforts from groin injury. Matthijs De Ligt had back surgery and won't recover in time. Xavi Simons out with torn ACL. Jerdy Schouten also unavailable with serious knee injury.

items.headline: Japan loses Minamino to ACL injury
items.body: Takumi Minamino suffered torn ACL in French Cup in December; failed to recover despite returning to training in March. Kazuki Endo ruptured ankle ligaments in February, now back on grass hoping to play before tournament. Takehiro Tomiyasu managing injuries.

items.headline: Star forwards missing due to injury
items.body: Brazil without Rodrygo and Estêvão. France without Hugo Ekitike. Japan without Mitoma (hamstring) and Minamino. Morocco dealt late blow losing Ezzalzouli to knee injury, replaced by Amine Sbaï. Germany's Serge Gnabry tore adductor. Austria's Christoph Baumgartner unavailable.

items.headline: USMNT dealt injuries despite depth
items.body: United States without Patrick Agyemang (Achilles) and Johnny Cardoso (ankle). Chris Richards initially doubtful with ankle injury but cleared Wednesday. Mauricio Pochettino has deepest roster in USMNT history but navigating injury management heading into Group D.

items.headline: Form-based omissions reshape competitions
items.body: Cole Palmer omitted by England despite recent Chelsea switch due to poor 2025-26 season. Phil Foden also suffered form slump and missed selection. Yunus Musah remains out of USMNT plans. Uruguay's Jose Gimenez managing high ankle sprain, expected available mid-tournament.

items.headline: Record 48 teams in expanded format
items.body: Tournament features 12 groups of four teams in round-robin format. Top two from each group plus eight best third-place teams advance to Round of 32. Each team plays three group matches. Format aims to reduce collusion risk versus earlier three-team group proposals.

items.headline: Squad sizes and registration deadlines
items.body: Each team submits maximum 26 players including three goalkeepers. Official squad confirmations by FIFA June 2. Late injury replacements allowed until 24 hours before team's first match if medical officers confirm severity. Haiti's Leverton Pierre replaced June 11.

items.headline: France leads with Mbappé firepower
items.body: Kylian Mbappé arrives as arguably the planet's best player with 41 goals across all competitions for Real Madrid. France squad includes established depth: N'Golo Kanté, Jules Koundé, Marcus Thuram. William Saliba fit after back concerns. Ranked third in FIFA standings.

metadata.mbappé_stats: 96 caps, 56 goals, 41 goals for Real Madrid 2025-26

items.headline: Spain favored despite Yamal concerns
items.body: Spain ranked second in FIFA standings with deep squad. Luis de la Fuente managing Yamal's fitness carefully; Barcelona prospect on track for Cape Verde opener June 15 but likely restricted minutes. Tournament broadcaster Fox ranked Yamal best player in tournament.

items.headline: Argentina defend as reigning champions
items.body: Defending champions feature Lionel Messi healthy after hamstring recovery. Messi scored in Iceland warm-up, completed training sessions normally. Argentina won both tune-ups convincingly with shutouts. Ranked first in FIFA standings.

items.headline: England, Portugal, Brazil round out elite
items.body: England ranked fourth; Portugal fifth; Brazil ranked sixth despite missing Rodrygo and Estêvão. England managing Saka's Achilles issue with monitor on minutes. Brazil's depth tested but Neymar return adds attacking dimension. Host advantage for USA with Pochettino's experienced squad.
